facts.text: Graniteville sits on the San Juan ridge between the Middle and South Forks of the Yuba River, about 26 miles northeast of Nevada City.
First settled in 1850, Graniteville was the original town in Eureka Township and an early gold‑mining center for Nevada County.
In 1867 a U.S. Post Office was established, officially changing the town’s name from Eureka to Graniteville to avoid confusion with another Eureka.
The town once hosted a brewery, bakery, saloons, and a livery stable, reflecting its bustling 19th‑century mining economy.
Graniteville was connected to the world’s first long‑distance telephone line in 1878, linking mining communities along the San Juan Ridge.
By 1855, enough children in Graniteville warranted opening a school, marking early community growth.
